title: The Cover of the Free Port Revisited
premise: Paloma Vane, a financial-crimes investigator who faked her own disappearance after 'the incident' at the Free Port, is living under a new name laundering clean money for a compliance firm. When a voiceprint she recorded years ago unlocks a hidden server in Singapore, her old identity resurfaces, dragging her into a three-government standoff over evidence that could topple the Free Port's protectors. Hunted by an assassin who once loved her, she must smuggle the truth across shifting borders and decide whether loyalty to the man who saved her matters more than the truth that damns him. In the end, she testifies at dawn, the assassin chooses love over the kill, and the checkpoint shifts change just as the truth crosses the line.
about_author: Quentin Galloway is the pen name of a former maritime compliance auditor who spent a decade tracing shell companies through duty-free zones before turning to fiction. He writes thrillers from a different coastal city every year, claiming that clean money is the most frightening subject he knows.

chapters.title: Clean Money
chapters.summary: POV: Paloma. Paloma Vane, living as 'Mara Quill,' audits spotless accounts at a Zurich compliance firm, unable to sleep through the night since the incident at the Free Port. A routine flag on a Singapore transfer shows her own voiceprint as an access key. The beat: dread disguised as routine.

chapters.title: The Voice in the Server
chapters.summary: POV: Paloma. She replays the voiceprint sample and recognizes her own recorded testimony from the night of the incident, evidence she believed destroyed. A dead drop message in the metadata names a Singapore data haven and a deadline tied to checkpoint shift changes. The beat: the past knocking.

chapters.title: What the Incident Was
chapters.summary: POV: Paloma, with a flashback interleave. Fragmented memory reconstructs the Free Port warehouse, her handler Aldous Renk, and the fire she may or may not have set. She realizes the server holds the full recording, not her edited version. The beat: unreliable memory turning against her.

chapters.title: Three Flags
chapters.summary: POV: alternating Paloma and an Interpol analyst, Dev Sarna. Sarna flags the voiceprint match independently; three governments open quiet files on 'the Quill anomaly.' Paloma books a flight under a third name. The beat: the noose of attention tightening from all sides.

chapters.title: The Man Who Was Sent
chapters.summary: POV: Ilya Ferro, the assassin. Ferro receives the contract: retrieve the server, eliminate the voice. He recognizes the voiceprint as Paloma, the woman he loved and lost at the Free Port, and requests the job personally. The beat: love weaponized into duty.

chapters.title: Departure Lounge
chapters.summary: POV: Paloma. At Zurich airport, Paloma spots Ferro's tradecraft in the terminal and realizes he's on her trail, not to kill her yet, but to herd her. She lets him, betting he still hesitates. The beat: dangerous trust in an old love.

chapters.title: Singapore, After Hours
chapters.summary: POV: Paloma. In Singapore's data haven, she reaches the server room but the voiceprint fails, altered. Ferro appears, disarms her, and instead of killing her, plays the first thirty seconds of the recording: her voice, confessing. The beat: betrayal inside tenderness.

chapters.title: Renk's Ledger
chapters.summary: POV: Ferro. Ferro's flashback reveals his employer: Aldous Renk, her old handler, who engineered the incident to bury the Free Port's real client. Ferro begins to doubt which of them was the weapon. The beat: loyalty curdling into doubt.

chapters.title: The Edited Woman
chapters.summary: POV: Paloma. Comparing the server recording with her memory, Paloma discovers her own recollection was chemically edited during the cover-up. She cannot trust the confession, the fire, or her love for Ferro. The beat: the ground of self dissolving.

chapters.title: Sarna's Dilemma
chapters.summary: POV: Dev Sarna. Sarna is ordered by his own government to bury the voiceprint match; the Free Port's protectors reach into Interpol. He goes off-book and sends Paloma a one-time cipher: 'The recording is the third copy. Find the first.' The beat: one honest man choosing truth.

chapters.title: The First Copy
chapters.summary: POV: Paloma. Following the cipher to a decommissioned Free Port annex in Rotterdam, Paloma finds the original analog tape hidden by a dead colleague, along with a note naming Renk's client: a joint state venture. The beat: the truth is bigger and worse than she feared.

chapters.title: Checkpoint
chapters.summary: POV: alternating Paloma and Ferro. At the Rotterdam border, Ferro corners her with orders to terminate. She offers him the tape and the choice: duty or the woman he loved. He lets her pass, and reports her 'eliminated.' The beat: love against duty, decided in ninety seconds.

chapters.title: Ghost Protocol
chapters.summary: POV: Renk. Renk, suspicious of Ferro's report, activates a second cleaner and begins scrubbing the Free Port's digital history, inadvertently confirming every claim on the tape. The beat: the villain's caution becoming his confession.

chapters.title: The Second Cleaner
chapters.summary: POV: Paloma. Paloma and Sarna regroup in a Rotterdam safehouse; the second cleaner, Voss, finds them. Sarna takes a bullet buying her escape, alive but broken, and the tape is nearly lost in the canal. The beat: the cost of truth made flesh.

chapters.title: What Ferro Knows
chapters.summary: POV: Ferro. Ferro intercepts Voss, realizing Renk will erase him too once the job closes. He brings Paloma his own evidence: Renk's kill ledger, her name on the last page. The beat: enemies becoming allies against a common handler.

chapters.title: Three Governments, One Room
chapters.summary: POV: Paloma. Paloma brokers a secret meeting with liaisons from all three governments, offering the tape in exchange for immunity and Renk's prosecution. Each government wants it buried differently; the meeting collapses into mutual accusation. The beat: institutions as the true antagonist.

chapters.title: The Long Night
chapters.summary: POV: Paloma and Ferro, alternating. Hiding in the Free Port itself, they wait out the night before the checkpoint shifts change, and for the first time since the incident, Paloma sleeps, in Ferro's watch. The beat: rest as surrender to trust.

chapters.title: Renk Comes Home
chapters.summary: POV: Renk and Paloma, alternating. Renk corners them in the warehouse where it all began, tape in hand, and offers Paloma the edited version of her own memory as mercy: forget, and live. She refuses. Ferro disarms him, but Renk triggers the facility's incineration protocol. The beat: the past demanding to be burned again.

chapters.title: Fire, Reversed
chapters.summary: POV: Ferro. Ferro carries the injured Renk out, choosing to save the man who ordered Paloma's death, so he can testify, while Paloma runs the tape to the duplication point through the burning annex. The beat: the incident replayed with a different ending.

chapters.title: Shift Change
chapters.summary: POV: Paloma. As the border checkpoint shifts change, Paloma crosses with the certified copies, Sarna's affidavit, and Ferro's ledger, minutes ahead of Voss and the second scrub team. The truth legally crosses the border before it can be killed. The beat: the race won by seconds.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: POV: Paloma. At the tribunal, Paloma testifies under her real name, the edited memory and the original tape played side by side. Renk is convicted; two governments fall into scandal; Sarna watches from the gallery. The beat: truth spoken aloud, finally whole.

chapters.title: The Cover of the Free Port
chapters.summary: POV: Paloma. Months later, Paloma sleeps through the night in a coastal city, her new name chosen rather than imposed. Ferro sends no message, only a postcard of the Free Port, now a museum. She keeps it. The beat: love and truth, both survived, neither fully resolved.
